releaseNotes: Platform release: someone can now be asked, by name, to look at a specific thing — a claim, a decision, a deliverable, one of its sections, or a workstream — and the ask stays open until they answer. A comment is addressed to nobody in particular; a review request names one person and one question, which is the difference between a workspace people can talk in and a workspace work moves through. What is waiting on the signed-in member appears first on Today, above anything the product worked out on its own about what they should do next.

The rule the feature is built to hold is that a review is an opinion, not an authority. Approving one changes nothing about the record it is about: it does not promote a deliverable, does not decide a decision, and does not move readiness. If it did, reviews would be a back door around the capability ladder — a reviewer who cannot edit a deliverable could settle one anyway by approving a review of it — and nobody would have had to open that door deliberately. Two identity rules the ladder cannot express live in the domain instead: only the person asked may answer, because an owner answering on a reviewer's behalf puts words in their mouth and whose opinion it is happens to be the whole value of the record; and only the person who asked may withdraw, because withdrawing someone else's ask decides for them that it needed no answer. Schema 7 adds the collection. Checks, 209 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
